project.title: Pitch Coach
project.medium: Singing trainer plugin – C++, JUCE (AU, VST3, standalone)
project.content:
A plugin that listens while you sing and shows how close you are to the note.

It tracks the pitch of the voice in real time and draws it against a guide melody on a piano-roll, in the key and scale of the song. Every held note gets its deviation in cents, and the panels above sum up the take: how many notes landed on target, how far off they were on average, and how quickly each note was reached. The previous take can stay visible for comparison.

caseStudy.role: Solo project – interface design, audio programming, code
caseStudy.challenge: I sing on my own music projects, and practising alone you can't hear yourself objectively. So I built the tool I wanted: one that shows how close you are to the note while you sing – and tells you afterwards what to work on.

decisions.title: Feedback while you sing
decisions.text: The voice is tracked in real time with the YIN pitch algorithm and drawn against a guide melody on a piano roll, in the key and scale of the song – so you see a wrong note the moment you sing it.

decisions.title: A summary after the take
decisions.text: Panels above the roll sum up each take in three numbers: notes on target, the average deviation in cents, and how quickly each note was reached.

decisions.title: Progress you can see
decisions.text: The previous take can stay visible underneath the new one, so improvement is something you compare, not something you guess.

caseStudy.result: A working plugin for any music program (AU, VST3) and a standalone app, written in C++ with JUCE, with a test for the take analysis. Source on GitHub.
